title: Real factorial series is summable
statement:
For every real number $x$, the real series
$$\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^r}{r!}$$
is summable, meaning that its net of sums over finite subsets of $\mathbf N$ converges to a real number; $0!=1$ and $x^0=1$ even when $x=0$. Convergence is for the usual absolute-value metric $d(x,y)=|x-y|$ on $\mathbf R$, with absolute value as in [def-weil-complex-absolute-value].
